label: input token g at original position >= 3
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is g during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 3 or later, and essentially nowhere else (precision 1.0 on dev). It is silent for g at positions 0-2, at the delimiter, and during the copy phase, including when g is fed back as an input or is the output. Magnitude rises with position: g at t=3 gives about 0.15-0.2 of max, and the top activations are all g at t=8, the last original slot of L=9 sequences. Firing rate is flat (~3.4%) across orig_idx 3-8, so mass share by position comes from magnitude, not from how often it fires. A repeated g also fires. Neighbouring tokens, first token and digit count have no notable effect. The only misses are 28 near-zero activations (<0.02 of max) on other tokens at t=8.

issues: No refutation found. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9994, F1 0.9997, mass recall 0.99998, with 0 false positives.

The 34 test misses carry 0.0% of the activation mass. All are at step 8 on tokens other than g (f, v, c, w, d, ...) with activations of 0.01-0.02 of max. This is the same scattered noise the explanation describes, not a systematic class.
The phase claims check out: 0 activations at the delimiter and 0 in the copy phase (out_tok g is never active). There are also 0 activations at t = 0-2.
The flat firing rate checks out: about 0.033-0.034 at each orig_idx from 3 to 8. Magnitude rises with position: g at t=3 sits around 0.15-0.17 of max, and the top 12 activations are all g at t=8.
Repeated g fires, e.g. 'g 0 n s k w [g:0.80] o [g:0.98]'. Previous token, first token and digit count all show flat lift.

Minor nuance the explanation leaves out: a repeat g sometimes has a lower activation than position alone would predict (e.g. g at t=3 then g at t=4 gives 0.16 then 0.41). This does not affect the label.
